There’s more than just a Hall of Mirrors.
I’ve heard rumors on the rapevine right next to Heaven’s Web there’s an entire world of them.
We’d climb it in our younger days — spend hours picking leaves off — the kind that we speculated would never break our fall — yet here we are today. Silent and scared.
Some might call it sleeping.
But me? I’ve always been the type to pull the petals off of whatever flowers we find in the garden. Preserve them in books so that one day, when I learn how to read, I can remember those moments.
The ones in which everything still felt young and new. Before we lost which part of the circle we were in. Now everything feels like a barrier and we can never figure out where we started.
In the beginning of someone’s end, there was little more than a ball of light.
Mercutio would tell you it’s no bigger than an alderman on the fore-finger of an agate stone.
But Mercutio is a liar — for I have decapitated the fairies’ midwife and placed the head of Queen Mab on a pike mere blocks from that rapevine we used to climb.
It is bigger now. Like us.
Which is probably why we never sleep at all anymore.
It’s dark beneath its shadow — and the world of mirrors reflects it every which way.
Tell me — what are you afraid of?
And where would you rest in a world made of mirrors?
: Wha-
: What the fuck is...where am...huh?!
One more light in the lamp — a mark on a list that grew like an ant-filled plant dancing with aunts on a ramp in a trance like an enchanted tramp clamp. So I start to recant but I can’t.
And I can’t recant because of the cramps. Because my clothes are too damp. So I plug my timestamp into an amp and get gassed as the downcast grass rushes half past the outcast mast.

Is it time to go to class? Never. This past surpassed cast hast been fast yet not vast. It’s a blast, this caste — full of masks and casks and masques and casques. But I just have one question to ask.
If Jack’s axe wants to fax some facts to the snack-shack in exchange for sacks but only receives tacks, does he tax the tacks or send them back due to cracks? It’s none of your beeswax.
Jack’s far too lax. He’s a failure, a quack. With a backpack full of Prozac and cognac that does naught but brush back the track I’ve been circling since this paragraph started.
I am far too old to be doing this here. I am far too young to feel fear.
But what I can do is hold your hands while you paint and try to catch the blues that never make it onto the canvas.

: Give you.............what you need.............
: Wha-
: I’m so proud of you, Yumi.
: Sensei?...
: You’re here too now?...
: What are you talking about? I’ve always been here. I’ve always been watching. Which is why I’m so proud of you.
: All that you’ve accomplished...all that you’ve worked for...you’ve come so far.
: And all it took was for your illness to be cured. To think it was something so simple that had been holding you back.
: But I’ve...I haven’t...
: I haven’t done anything! Anything at all! I’ve barely changed since-
: Just think...how much would you be capable of if you took even more?
: I wish that could be me — so unbothered by the world around me that it’s barely even a factor.
: I admire you. No...
: I love you, Yumi.
: Please — accept these. These are my body. Take it and eat. Take it and become a better you.
: Am I not good enough the way I am now?...Outside of this...surreal fantasy you’ve all pulled me into?
: Of course not. No one is.
: Which is why we must rely on other things. Which is why we hide ourselves in what we do or who we do.
: But can you imagine a world where you and I could be that for each other?
: No...I can’t...
: Then take me and eat me. Make it possible.
: Everything you could ever need is right there in your hands.
: Happy birthday, Yumi. We’ve been waiting for you.
: Come. Fill your hands with the candy we’ve so gleefully gathered and dumped into these festive bowls for you.
: I picked them out myself.
: What’s the matter? Haven’t you ever seen two talking faces on a chalkboard in the dark before?
: As a matter of fact, I can’t say I have.
: Don’t mind Right Face — he’s always been a bit of a joker. Regardless, won’t you celebrate with us?
: We’ve waited so very long for you, after all.
: Even when the others told us not to.
: Shh. She doesn’t need to know about that.
: You two know my birthday isn’t until Halloween, right?...It’s the middle of June right now.
: It’s always Halloween in here.
: Which means that every day, you’ll grow some more. Numerically and mentally. Mostly numerically. That number would grow quite large rather quickly, wouldn’t it?
: But where is here?...What is this place? And where did my mom go? Where did Sensei go?!
: Dead, presumably. They’d have existed thousands of years ago at this point.
: The fuck do you mean “thousands of years ago?!” How am I still here then?!
: Time doesn’t move here. At least not in the traditional sense.
: We came up with our own calendar because time is a man-made construct, then rearranged it to have every day as October 31st — the human Halloween.
: We’ve also extended days to what would be considered about thirty hours each where you’re from so that everyone can get eight hours of sleep.
: But no one ages. And everything outside of here is exactly the same as it has always been.
: Probably. We’re two faces on a chalkboard, so all we know is what we’ve heard from others.
: There are...others?...
: Your entire family is here. Those who came after, at least.
: Hundreds and hundreds of descendants — each with your eyes. And they all have a piece of you in them.
: Mostly due to inbreeding. But we’d be lying if we said the vast majority didn’t also have some sort of genetic makeup causing them to act like delinquents more often than not.
: So you two are...like...
: Gods, I suppose you’d call us.
: Very specific and very weak ones. But gods nonetheless.
: I am Migi, the God of Chalk.
: And I am Hidari, the God of Black-Haired Tsundere Girls.
: You can be a god too, you know.
: You practically already are. The others here view you as such anyway. You just need to ascend.
: And fill out the appropriate paperwork.
: Migi can help with that. He is the God of Chalk after all.
: So what do you say, Yumi? Will you stay?
: Will you celebrate your birthday with us?
: We’ll wait as long as it takes.
: Go on — help yourself to some candy in the meantime.
: Yeah, uh...
: Thanks, but I’m...not really into the whole “god” thing.
: Not even me? But I’m so specifically tailored to you. What else would you rather believe?
: I don’t know. Nothing, I guess?
: But if you don’t believe in anything-
